title: Route development requests by risk and enforce a friction budget

requirement.summary: Replace universal per-task confirmation with a vendor-neutral router that observes no-write requests without task admission, fast-tracks bounded low-risk proposals under explicit standing human policy, reuses active admitted work without repeated confirmation, and reserves review for real ambiguity or material risk.

objective.rationale: The structured admission fallback is safe but becomes product drift if every question, diagnosis, trivial change, and in-scope iteration must stop for a full preview and special confirmation word. AgentGov should route all observed work but interrupt humans only at material boundaries.

goal: Add strict standing-policy, structured work-request, and routing-result contracts plus a CLI/library flow that deterministically chooses observe-only, continue-active, policy fast-track, human review, or full review, and permits non-interactive low-risk task creation only when an admitted human policy explicitly delegates it.
non_goals: Do not make every user request create a development task or require a manual confirmation.
Do not infer request meaning, risk, scope, or authority directly from raw prompts, transcripts, assistant responses, source bodies, credentials, models, or host paths.
Do not let Coding Agent classification alone grant fast-track authority; authority must come from a strict repository policy admitted by an accountable human.

Do not fast-track ambiguous scope, unknowns, medium/high/critical risk, architecture changes, dependency changes, authentication/authorization, security boundaries, data schema or migration, destructive operations, external writes, infrastructure/deployment, public API compatibility, or policy changes.
Do not automatically start or replace a development session, execute validation, change code, expand scope, approve an exception, or perform Git, publication, deployment, or release actions.
Do not add a hidden daemon, vendor-specific Core fields, a second host Adapter, or a cryptographic human-identity claim.
Do not commit, push, merge, publish, release, deploy, install a host component, or write to an external system.
acceptance_signals: A strict vendor-neutral work-request contract classifies no-write work, new repository changes, and active-task continuation without carrying raw conversation or authority fields; material-risk flags are explicit and unknown fields fail closed.

A strict human-owned standing admission policy declares allowed no-write classes, whether low-risk fast-track is enabled, allowed scope prefixes and validation command prefixes, maximum scope/validation/risk-item counts, forbidden material characteristics, and a numeric friction budget.

Routing is deterministic and produces observe-only for allowed no-write requests, continue-active only for a locally verified active admitted task with matching identity, fast-track only when every policy constraint passes, human review for bounded low-risk proposals outside delegation, and full review for material or ambiguous work.

The friction budget requires zero manual confirmations for no-write observation, policy fast-track, and active-task continuation, at most one for ordinary bounded review, and explicit full review for material work; route results report the applicable budget and actual planned confirmations.

Policy-authorized fast-track apply works non-interactively, revalidates policy/proposal/route digests and exclusive target safety, creates only the exact reviewed compact task, and does not create a session/event or execute validation.
Without a valid admitted policy, or when policy/request/proposal/active-task facts drift, the router fails closed to review and never writes or overwrites a task.

Existing exact ADMIT fallback, task proposal, host interaction, Coding Agent cards, JSONL, Codex Hook, coordinator, session, task, scope, completion, packaging, and repository behavior remains compatible.
Focused tests, the complete Python 3.11 suite, task/scope/repository checks, schema parsing, packaging assertions, and diff checks pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_admission_routing tests.test_task_proposal tests.test_coding_agent_transport tests.test_host_interaction tests.test_development_session tests.test_task_contract -v

items: A weak or agent-controlled policy could turn fast-track into self-authorization.
A false low-risk classification could bypass a necessary human review.
Universal routing overhead could still become user-visible bureaucracy if no-write and active-task cases are not genuinely zero-confirmation.
A policy or proposal race could create a different task from the one evaluated by the route.

stop_conditions: Stop if fast-track authority can originate from the Coding Agent request, a command flag, environment variable, inferred intent, or host permission instead of an admitted repository policy.

Stop if any material-risk flag, ambiguity, unknown, unsafe scope, unrestricted validation command, policy mismatch, drift, or missing local active-task fact can still produce fast-track or continue-active.
Stop if no-write or active-task routing creates a task, writes repository state, or requires a manual confirmation.
Stop if fast-track apply writes anything beyond the exact reviewed task file, overwrites a target, starts a session, appends an event, or executes a command.
Stop if the implementation claims terminal presence proves human identity or claims static classification proves semantic correctness.
Stop before any Git write, host installation, release, consumer mutation, deployment, or external-system write.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the completed risk router, confirmed that human decisions should remain while manual input is minimized, and explicitly authorized the proactive minimal-input decision experience as the next requirement on 2026-08-06.
